reason: This text fragment (Exodus 2:16-22) describes a personal encounter between Moses and Jethro's daughters at a well in Midian. The narrative is entirely domestic: the daughters water their flocks, shepherds drive them away, Moses helps them, and he subsequently marries Zipporah. The passage explicitly identifies the location as a foreign land (אֶרֶץ נָכְרִיָּה), not Hebrew territory. There is no portrayal of the Hebrew nation, no political struggle, and no fight for liberty—only an individual's personal circumstances and family relations during his exile.
